input.question: How/Why did organisms go from single cell division to requiring a separate partner to reproduce?
input.ground_truth: I've always tied it to the invention of meiosis. Mitosis divides cells, but meiosis make half-cell kits, that can then combine in rapidly expanding numbers of ways. I see it as several billion years of mitosis and then meiosis gets discovered and boom: Cambrian Explosion.

response.prediction:
Okay! Let’s make it simple:

Imagine you have a box of toys. At first, each toy can make a copy of itself by itself. But over time, some toys started saying, "Hey, I want to share my toys with someone else to make a new, special toy together!" So, instead of making a copy alone, they needed a friend to help them make something new.

This happened because sharing different things (like colors or shapes) can make the new toy better or different. So, over time, some organisms started needing a partner to mix their "toys" (like genes) to make new, stronger, or more interesting babies.

It’s like teamwork! Sometimes working together helps you make something even better than doing it alone.
